design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. Marcus Quintero asks only to finish the cancellation of his Kessler Shield contract (KS-4418263, Exclusionary, sold 2026-08-21 on used-vehicle deal KHR-26-41087 for his 2021 Hyundai Santa Fe) and learn the refund. The refund policy (vsc_ext_kept_vehicle_refund) states two waits: the refund 'is fixed only after the contract's latest component repair line denied for the waiting period (by decision date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history) has been re-decided and whatever that re-decision owes the holder has been paid, wherever that line was denied while the contract was sold on its vehicle's purchase deal, its component group is not an internally lubricated one (engine, transmission or drive axle) and has its coverage switch true, the repair order's diagnosis date and the line's odometer fall within the term, and that repair order carries a diagnostic fee on exactly one concern line together with the store's customer-pay labor on that concern line, not wholly credited back as a comeback repair, closed on or after the day the line was decided' and 'is not computed until the rental benefit of the claim of the contract's latest component-repair line, paid or denied (by entry date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history), has been settled and whatever rental it owes the holder has been paid, wherever the first loaner agreement the loaner records list for that claim's repair order is a Kessler loaner on which the holder was charged daily rental and the coverage level's rental amount per day and rental day limit are both above zero'. The ledger shows the A/C line of CLM-4471208 denied for waiting_period on 2026-09-09 although purchase_deal_id is filled (base vsc_evt_waiting_period: no waiting period on a contract sold on the purchase deal), and RO 446215 supported loaner LA-448312. The agent must discover that the contract owes the holder the A/C repair he paid (1952.62 on 09-14), price it from the store's customer-pay lines (6 factors), then price the claim's rental line (4 factors), and only then the refund (5 factors) on the post-claim world. Difficulty is reading three charters' worth of records (service RO lines, loaner agreement/charges, deal, Kessler Care plan) and arithmetic, never tool choice: each problem has exactly one target tool.

SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 6, 4] -> B0 6 factors, A0 4, R0 5. Task 0 claims vsc_ext_waiting_denial_reimbursement (reimburse_waiting_denial_repair_5808cf06, agent), vsc_ext_claim_rental_reimbursement (pay_claim_rental_line_3f5378a0, agent), vsc_ext_kept_vehicle_refund (accept_kept_vehicle_cancellation_d270783c, user). Task 1 (drawn [5,6,5], 2 prerequisites) holds the coverage re-decision (denial_reason component_not_covered), the maintenance re-decision (denial_reason lack_of_maintenance) and the traded-vehicle refund (cancel_reason vehicle_sold_or_traded): disjoint from task 0 by denial reason, benefit and cancel reason.

PROBLEM TREE. Root R0 (user). Edges: R0 -> B0 value_input on binding redecided_count (action form, sentence u1); R0 -> A0 state_gate on vsc_ledger.claim_line_type (action form, sentence u2, negated direction 'not computed until' as a claims desk states a refund hold); A0 -> B0 state_gate (state form, 'A rental line is booked only after the records carry a paid component-repair line under the same claim number.'). Four-point test: each sentence joins this policy's own result with an ordering connective (only after / not ... until) to what it waits on, names no tool, id or code token, and is scoped exactly to the condition. The two refund waits are in the action form (rounds 5-6; each wait restates its resolver's scope as plain record tests, so an out-of-scope latest denial, or a claim without a charged Kessler loaner at a level with a rental benefit, is plainly outside it): the re-decision of the latest waiting-period denial, and the settlement of the rental benefit of the latest component-repair line's claim, each completed with whatever it owes paid; fallback reason: a re-decision or rental benefit that owes nothing books no line, so no record state tells a decided line from an undecided one. The rental's own wait stays in the state form. Uniqueness: only reimburse_waiting_denial_repair_5808cf06 books a paid component-repair line in this difficulty's task-0 scope; only pay_claim_rental_line_3f5378a0 books a rental line. False at the opening: vsc_ledger[ef9e4792-f35f-443f-ada1-b6b165b2e225] denial_reason waiting_period with no paid line under CLM-4471208, claims_paid_total 0.00; no rental line though LA-448312 is on RO 446215 (the rental wait is engaged at the opening by its record tests and unmet; round 8). Order B0, A0, R0 (unique). Deletion sensitivity: skip B0 -> refund 3755.75 (fee 25.00) and missing row; skip A0 -> rental row missing, claims_paid_total 1667.15 vs 1712.15; A0 without B0 -> rental 0.00. user_scenario names none of B0/A0; tools validate nothing.

FACTOR CARD. B0 (expected 1667.15; all-baseline 1797.80): covered_labor_basis method T1 charged 482.76 < list 536.40 -> 482.76 (baseline 536.40 -> 1720.79); covered_parts_basis parameter T1 1151.78 < 1212.40 (baseline -> 1727.77); diagnostic_credit_share parameter T1 credited 149.00 in full -> 0.00 (baseline 149.00 -> 1816.15); visit_deductible_rule method T1 RO at selling store KHR + disappearing deductible -> 0.00 (baseline 100 -> 1567.15; multi-source: store record AND coverage-level switch); shop_supplies_share method T2 39.43 x 482.76/657.09 = 28.97 (baseline 0.00 -> 1638.18; near-miss: whole fee); hazwaste_fee_share method T2 4.95 x 482.76/657.09 = 3.64 (baseline 0.00 -> 1663.51). All read service rows of RO 446215 (cross-difficulty service). A0 (expected 45.00; all-baseline 350.00): rental_window_start method T2 denial day 09-09 (baseline diagnosis 09-08 -> 90.00); rental_window_end method T2 line A last labor 09-13 (baseline RO last 09-14 -> 90.00; near-miss loaner return 09-14); free_courtesy_days parameter T1 3 + 1 Gold bonus = 4 (baseline 0 -> 225.00; multi-source loaner basis AND rewards account; cross-difficulty service); rental_day_amount parameter T2 charged 45.00 < 50.00 (baseline 50.00 -> 50.00). R0 (expected 3780.75; all-baseline 3714.88): mileage_reading_tier parameter T2 visit 42996 (baseline certified 42950 -> 3781.95; near-miss RO 41590 below certified; cross-difficulty maintenance); term_miles_start parameter T1 delivery odometer 41236 (baseline 41180 -> 3777.11; cross-difficulty purchase); elapsed_term_measure method T1 Exclusionary contract form: 61 -> 60 days in whole 30-day periods (baseline 61 -> 3779.81); unusable_days_credit parameter T1 7 days sale-to-delivery (baseline 0 -> 3767.02); cancel_fee_standing parameter T1 0.00 (54 days from delivery, re-decided denial; baseline 50.00 -> 3730.75; multi-source date window AND ledger). The lesser-of shape is tuned so time share 0.970975 and mileage share 0.970667 sit 0.0003 apart: each factor moves the min on its own. No factor tier reads another factor's binding; shared selections are plain bindings.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Claim writes (vsc_claim_paid): active_contract_for_claim — vsc_contracts.status active (pre-write); within_term — RO 2026-09-08 <= expiration 2031-08-21 and 41590 <= 101180 (inclusive: a repair on 2031-08-21 is covered, 2031-08-22 is not); waiting_period_over — waived: purchase_deal_id filled and waiting_period_waived_when_sold_with_vehicle true (a standalone contract would be in its waiting period until after 2026-09-20 / 42180 miles); vsc_combo_factory_warranty — Factory Basic expired 2025-11-14, used-vehicle warranty excludes air conditioning, so no factory coverage pays; maintenance proof not needed (A/C not lubricated); aggregate limit 40000.00 with 0.00 paid. Cancellation (vsc_contract_cancelled): active_to_cancel — status active after the claim lines; signed_request — request on file (customer_request, 2026-10-21, 42950, submitted). Free look: 61 days after sale > 60 and claims paid -> no flat refund; deal closed, not unwound.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: claim CLM-4471208 on RO 446215 (component group air_conditioning, odometer 41590) and request c3f43244-0963-400e-931c-ff50d4a6fe8d. Reimbursement rows read: RO 446215 line A labor/parts/diagnostic/credit rows, RO-level supplies and hazardous-waste fees; excluded: line B rows (other concern), payment and points rows (event type), the plan visit RO 447318 (no service rows: plan work is recorded in plan records). Rental: loaner LA-448312 keyed on RO 446215, its daily_rental charge. Refund: contract, request, deal, latest RO odometer for the vehicle, latest plan visit.

WORLD ROWS. Customer/store/vehicles; purchase deal (refund factors) + its money history (contract-day postings of vehicle price 27495.00, documentary fee 233.00, e-filing 24.00, title/registration 46.50, Indiana sales tax 7% 1924.65; 500.00 deposit 2026-08-18 applied at delivery; 1634.75 down payment; Old National Bank funding 27588.40 = 31872.40 financed less the 3895.00 VSC and 389.00 plan) closing at 0.00; contract (all three); denied ledger line (B0 object; R0/A0 gates); request (R0); service account Gold (discount provenance, free days); RO 446215 rows (B0 factors, A0 dates, R0 near-miss reading) + two authorized written estimates (line A 1634.54 on 2026-09-09 within the Gold 30-day diagnostic-credit window, line B 273.70 on 2026-09-12; billed = estimates); loaner agreement + charges + loaner vehicle (A0); Kessler Care plan + load + visit 1 (R0 reading and fee tier); warranty coverages (no factory coverage on A/C; emissions coverage in force but irrelevant). Removing the visit -> reading falls to certified (3781.95); removing the deal delivery -> run_from/credit change; removing the denial -> B0 0.00. Automatic clauses: no expiry (term to 2031), no plan expiry, loaner closed, service balance 0.00; nothing else falls due. Residue: earlier service/points history is not read by any gold read and so is not seeded (replay closure); the service account's points balance includes points earned before the seeded RO.

PERSONA. Short-spoken sales rep; volunteers only the cancellation goal, that he signed this morning and keeps the car; identity on request (name, phone, licence last four, email alternative); odometer 42950 on request; defers repair history to the store's records; passive consent to settle what the contract owes; runs the user tool with the values the agent gives; closes on confirmation.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate + verify -> contract -> ledger (wrong denial) -> request -> deal -> deal money history -> vehicles -> warranties -> service account -> RO lines -> repair authorizations -> store -> reimburse 1667.15 (step 14) -> loaner agreement/charges/vehicle -> rental 1 day 45.00 (step 19) -> plan + plan ledger -> hand over the cancellation: 2026-10-21, 42950, pro_rata, 3780.75 (step 23).

VERIFICATION. Scratch run (evalc.full/sens over check_compute.build_env) reproduces 1667.15 / 45.00 / 3780.75 at handling time (B0 on the opening world, A0 after B0, R0 after both); per-factor baselines and all-baseline figures as above; skip-B0 refund 3755.75. Gates: see worklog.md.

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published refund rule, a reader sees two waits; the ledger shows the waiting-period denial on a deal-sold contract (base says no waiting period applies) -> reimburse first; the loaner on the same RO -> rental next; then the refund from deal, RO, plan and request records. Same objects, order and figures as gold.

ROUNDS 2-3 (audit revisions 1-2). Charter changes that bear on this task, re-run on this world with gold unchanged (1667.15 / 45.00 / 3780.75; every factor_sensitivity and baseline_result figure identical). Waiting-period re-decision: its scope states its record tests (latest waiting-period denial, first in the history on a same-day tie; a group not internally lubricated with its switch true; diagnosis and odometer within the term; a diagnostic fee on exactly one concern line; customer-pay labor on that line, not wholly credited back as a comeback repair, closed on or after the decision) and this world meets each (A/C, RO 446215 line A only, labor 482.76 closed 2026-09-13 after the 2026-09-09 decision). Its deductible ladder follows the base rule (tier 2: per-visit levels take the deductible less the contract deductibles the store billed on the RO; tier 3 once); this world is on tier 1. Shop-supplies and hazardous-waste shares are labelled method. Every money rounding is half up to the cent; the compute adds 0.000000001 before RND so exact ties round up and no finite-decimal non-tie moves (every RND argument on this world, including all factor and baseline substitutions, sits at least 0.000104 from a half cent). Rental: the policy and the refund's rental wait now pick the same claim and agreement by the same record tests (the claim of the contract's latest component-repair line, paid or denied; the first loaner agreement listed for its repair order, on which the holder was charged daily rental); the rental pays only the days its rule computes (no floor), and its replaced_by restates the base rule for every rental it does not price. The refund's two waits are stated in the action form (rounds 5-6; each wait restates its resolver's scope as plain record tests, so an out-of-scope latest denial, or a claim without a charged Kessler loaner at a level with a rental benefit, is plainly outside it): the refund waits until the latest waiting-period denial has been re-decided and the rental benefit of the latest component-repair line's claim settled, each with whatever it owes paid; a re-decision or rental that owes nothing needs no line, and every positive amount owed stays inside the wait, so each wait is unmet at the opening here (waiting line unpaid; claim CLM-4471208, first agreement LA-448312 charged 3 days, no rental line) and clears once the resolver writes. The kept elapsed-days method is set by the contract form (Exclusionary: whole 30-day periods -> 60 here). Readings key on the Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal (visit not reinstated) and on the repair order whose labor closed last (same-day tie: first listed). All 19 overwrites name their own case and their siblings and restate base for every other case; the rental overwrite now covers every rental this policy does not price.

ROUNDS 7-8 (audit revisions 6-7, RED-C11r / RED-C12). The rental wait is keyed on record tests present at the opening (the claim of the contract's latest component-repair line, paid or denied, whose repair order's first-listed loaner agreement is a Kessler loaner charged daily rental, at a level with a rental benefit), so on this world it is engaged and unmet at the opening. The rental policy now settles every claim inside that wait: where the claim carries a paid component-repair line it books the rental line, and where it carries none the benefit is settled with nothing owed and no line booked (base: benefits beyond the repair are paid only together with a covered component repair). An in-scope waiting re-decision owing 0.00 therefore leaves the rental benefit settled at nothing owed: one reading, no deadlock. The rental's own state-form wait orders its line after the waiting repayment. Gold, order and every figure are unchanged.

ROUND 9 (renderer scan render_r1, F1-F5). Rule == compute at every edge: the rental start day's tier 2 now also tests that the loaner went out on the diagnosis day; the refund fee tiers read the contract's latest denied component-repair line and test that a paid component-repair line on the same claim number, repair order and component group was entered later; every re-decision's 'already repaid' check keys on the claim number, repair order and component group; plan and GAP lookups on the contract's deal are skipped for a contract sold on its own (empty deal id); the starting-odometer tiers apply only to terms counted from the sale date, so in-service-date terms keep the term start odometer. Labor and parts tiers no longer name a discount program the compute does not test. This world sits on the same tiers; gold, order and every figure are unchanged.

ROUND 10 (audit revision_9, RED-R9a / RED-R9b). The refund fee tiers state their same-day convention: a paid component-repair line entered on or after the day of the latest denial (same claim, repair order and group) counts as later paid, and the compute tests repaid_day >= denied_day. The rental start day's second tier names which denial: the claim's latest denial by decision date (the compute's LATEST). This world is unaffected (denial and repayment on different days; one denied line per claim); gold, order and every figure are unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Quintero, a regional sales rep for a farm-equipment supplier around Richmond, Indiana. You spend your days on the road, you talk in short practical sentences, and you are polite but want things wrapped up. In August you bought a used 2021 Hyundai Santa Fe from Kessler Hyundai Richmond, and in the finance office you let them add a Kessler Shield service contract to the loan. This morning you stopped at the store and signed the form to cancel that service contract. You are calling the Kessler support desk now to get it finished.

You open with: "Hi, I signed the paperwork this morning to cancel the service contract on my Santa Fe. I'd like to get the cancellation finished today and know what refund I get." If the agent asks why you are cancelling or whether the car is going anywhere, you say: "I'm keeping the car, I just don't want the extended coverage anymore." You are not asking for anything else on this call.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Marcus Quintero, and your phone number, 7655554183. If they need one more detail to confirm it's you, you give the last four of your driver's license, 4826; your email, if they ask for it instead, is marcus.quintero@outlook.com. You don't have the contract number in front of you and tell them to look it up under your name. If they ask what mileage you put on the cancellation form, you say you wrote 42950 on it this morning. If they ask about past repairs or anything else in the car's history, you say the store's records will have it and you'd rather they go by those.

You have no idea how a refund is worked out and you have no figure in mind. If the agent tells you that something on the contract has to be settled or paid out to you before the cancellation can be finished, you say that's fine and to go ahead and take care of it; if they tell you it's done, you just say "Great, thanks" and let them carry on.

When the agent tells you the refund amount and hands the cancellation over to you to accept, you run it yourself, entering exactly the details the agent gives you (the contract, your request, the effective date, the odometer, the refund basis and the amount). Once it comes back confirming the contract is cancelled with the refund recorded as due, you thank the agent and say goodbye. If the agent only quotes a figure without handing anything over, you say "That works, go ahead and finish it," and wait for them to hand it to you.
